pr_title: e2e daemon set: better polling in CheckDaemonStatus
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

As a quick fix for a flake, bceec5a3ffd6975105f95b08641e45644c0a6753 introduced polling with wait.Poll in all callers of CheckDaemonStatus.

This commit reverts all callers to what they were before (CheckDaemonStatus + ExpectNoError) and implements polling according to E2E best practices (https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-testing/writing-good-e2e-tests.md#polling-and-timeouts):

- no logging while polling
- support for progress reporting while polling
- last but not least, produce an informative failure message in case of a timeout, including a dump of the daemon set as YAML

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Related-to: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128054/commits/bceec5a3ffd6975105f95b08641e45644c0a6753#r1799565485
Fixes: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/128049

Discussed this with Antonio and Patrick on slack, we'll most likely try to align the 2 checks here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/faf89fe5e93b13c46e3dd6c14dec2708d35dc0d9/test/e2e/apps/daemon_set.go#L225-L227

The first one (in line 227) is polling directly pods to get the running ones, whereas the latter (in line 229) checks the daemon set status. One potential solution would be to align both checks to rely on the same value instead, or introduce polling in the latter. I'll work on potential solutions this week.

review_comments:
Nit: but I'd probably move the timeout information to the caller, so that the fact this function doesn't check just once but waits up to timeout is more readable. Probably something we'll want to fix at some later time. 
I agree and tried to address this with function documentation - but that's not ideal.

We don't have a good API pattern for optional function parameters. In e2epod, we ended up with lots of variants which just differ by the number and type of parameters. I think we should come up with something better, I just don't know yet what it is.
Actually, e2epod has one such pattern: provide building blocks (get function, gomega matcher) and let the caller decide how to put them together.

In this case, the call could look like this:
```
gomega.Eventually(ctx, e2edaemonset.Get(f, ds)).[WithTimeout(...)].Should(e2edaemonset.HaveAllPodsReady)
```
This is similar to the "return function for wait.Poll` approach from Antonio, except that it is for Gomega and more modular (getting the daemon set and assertions against it are separate).
